description:
Shocking footage shows helicopters crash into each other in Nepal

#news #crash #helicopter #nepal #everest 

This is the shocking moment two helicopters collided during landing, killing one tourist and injuring several others in Nepal.
Footage shows the aircraft operated by Fishtail Air and Dynasty Air crashing into each other at Pheriche Helipad in Solukhumbu earlier today.
The collision occurred at around 8:11 am local time in Ward 4 of Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality.
Bystanders, trekking tourists and ground crew members can be seen fleeing as debris scatters across the landing area

description:

title: Giant cruise liner SS United States is sunk to create world’s biggest artificial reef
description:
The SS United States has been sunk off the coast of Florida to create the world’s largest artificial reef.

The one-time world’s fastest liner was retired more than 50 years ago and has numerous failed attempts at restoration while being docked in Philadelphia.

Okaloosa County bought the 990-foot vessel in 2024 and sank it on Wednesday (November 11), 25 miles off the Florida coast between Panama City and Pensacola, to create a haven for divers and a home for local marine wildlife.

title: BREAKING: All US flights grounded due to “safety and communication issues” | BBC News
description:
All flights in the US have been grounded due to "extraordinary circumstances" relating to air traffic control communication issues. 

US Federal Aviation Administration  issued an order to ground all flights "for reasons of safety”.

The US Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said the issue had hit air traffic control centres and "FAA technicians are investigating the issue. We will provide immediate updates as we have them”.

The US Secretary for Homeland Security has said there was no indication of any kind of threat to the United States and the emergency is not due to terrorism or a cyber attack

title: Stuart Macgill's New "Danger Ball"...
description:
No, not really a new delivery but, for fear of getting it wrong, I've decided to title this video with the name the commentator has monkiered it.

My opinion, I think this is effectively the Shane Warne slider but bowled with the seam as the axis of spin (rather that the seam scrambled like warne's)

It's like an askew leg break; the angle at which the delivery is released means it has leg spin but is spinning backwards too. 

As the ball lands on the seam, it grips on the pitch. The leg spin on the ball means it turns... but the askew, back-spinning action means it only turns fractionally.
